scenario.title: Late shipments
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

F-01.statement: 300 out of 1000 orders are late at handover stage

F-02.statement: Median pickup delay is 2.0 hours based on 60 pickups

F-03.statement: 21 failed runs out of 30 for RELEASE-BATCH job; 290 orders released after pickup.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

interpretation_history.interpretation: 300 out of 1000 orders are late at the handover stage, showing a 30% lateness rate. This quantifies the symptom at a specific process step.
The pickup log shows a median delay of 2.0 hours across 60 pickups, indicating a measurable delay at the pickup stage that could contribute to late orders.

E-03.content: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation attributes parcel lateness to carrier pickup delays of two hours, suggesting that the carrier's schedule is a contributing factor to late shipments.
The release batch job shows a high failure rate (21/30 runs) and many orders (290) released after pickup, indicating a process issue that could contribute to late shipments.

E-05.content: Carrier contract §3: pickup schedule changes run after SH-CAR confirms.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The carrier contract stipulates that any pickup schedule change can only proceed after the carrier account manager (SH-CAR) confirms it. This shows that schedule adjustments are gated by carrier approval, aligning with the existing K-SCHED constraint.

current_plan.rationale: Measure handover lateness (E-01) and notify carrier so pickup schedule can be adjusted, addressing the root cause of carrier pickup delay (E-02, E-03) that drives the 30% lateness rate. Evidence: E-01 shows 30% lateness at handover; E-02 shows median pickup delay of 2.0 h; E-03 attributes lateness to carrier pickup delay. This directly supports the release‑scope items track_lateness_at_handover and alert_carrier_of_delay, which are CORE_FEATURE work needed to verify and mitigate the root cause. Side effect: Additional read load on order-db and pickup-log; alert notifications generate communication overhead. Reversibility: Work items are read‑only queries and notifications; they mutate no state, so they are trivially reversible. Alternatives: (1) Omit carrier alerts and rely solely on monitoring; (2) Adjust pickup schedule without measurement (risk of mis‑alignment). (R-15)

proposal.summary: Carrier pickup delays of about 2 hours cause orders to be late at the handover stage, leading to a 30% lateness rate.
key_points: Evidence shows 300 out of 1000 orders are late at handover (E-01) and the median pickup delay is 2.0 hours (E-02); stakeholder input attributes lateness to carrier pickup (E-03) while release batch failures are not a major factor (E-04).
